Recording happens at two Gila County counters: Globe, which is the seat, and Payson, which is the biggest town. Each is staffed Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

OfficeAddressPhoneFax
GlobeGila County Courthouse, 1400 E Ash St, Globe, AZ 85501(928) 402-8740(928) 425-9270
PaysonTommie Cline Martin Complex, 707 S Colcord Rd, Payson, AZ 85541(928) 474-7139(928) 472-5346

The Payson counter closes on the fourth Tuesday of every month, so check the calendar before you drive. The same department that records your deed also keeps voter registration files current.

Fraud Notify is a free service from the Gila County Recorder's Office. It sends you a notice any time a document is recorded in your name. The county promotes it as protection against property fraud, since you hear about a bogus deed or lien right away.

A vacant or inherited house is where this helps most, since nobody is there to notice odd mail. Sign up from the county's Recorder page.

Most papers cost $30 to record, a price fixed in A.R.S. 11-475. Federal, state and local government requests pay $15. Each copied page is $1, and the Recorder's certificate and seal on a certified copy adds $3. Treat these as the starting point and ask the Recorder, or the title company handling your closing, for the exact total on your paperwork.

sections.h2: Transfers that skip the affidavit of legal value
sections.html:
Some transfers never need the buyer and seller affidavit. A.R.S. 11-1134 spells out which ones, and whichever applies must be written on the face of the deed. Families in Gila County meet these most often:

  • Gifts, and quitclaim deeds signed for no money.
  • Transfers a court has ordered.
  • Leases and easements, whatever their length.
  • Corrective deeds that confirm or fix one already on record.
  • Trustee's deeds under a deed of trust, plus transfers made only to secure or release a debt.
  • Token-price transfers of a residence among spouses, parents and children, grandparents and grandchildren, or siblings.
  • Beneficiary-deed transfers for nominal consideration.
  • Delinquent tax or assessment sales, partitions, and transfers that follow a legal name change.

Selling your house to an unrelated buyer for a real price is not on the list, so expect to fill out the affidavit. It records the price, the financing, the parcel number and the buyer's plans for the home.

sections.h2: Why the Recorder rejects a document
sections.html:
State law limits the reasons a recorder can turn a paper away. Under A.R.S. 11-480 the problems are a missing caption, a copy instead of an original, poor legibility, missing original signatures, a page bigger than 8.5 by 14 inches, or type under ten point. Reserve two inches at the top of page one for the recording stamp, and leave half an inch on the sides and bottom.

A paper that amends an earlier one must give the earlier recording date and its docket and page. If the first page fails the top margin test, a cover sheet carrying the title of the document fixes it.

A.R.S. 11-1133 requires the recorder to refuse a deed or sales contract with an incomplete affidavit, unless the paper notes a legal exemption. An affidavit is complete when every item is answered or marked not applicable.

Foreclosures have their own rule. When the beneficiary of a foreclosed trustee's deed receives an extra payment from private mortgage insurance, it must file a declaration with the County Recorder within four months of the trustee's sale. The declaration lists the parcel number, the beneficiary, the sale date, the highest bid, the recording number and the extra amount received within three months. If your house has a foreclosure in its chain of title, your title company will already know about this filing.

sections.h2: From closing table to public record
sections.html:
A sale reaches the Recorder only after several smaller steps are finished. Knowing the order helps you ask the right questions at the right time.

  1. You and the buyer sign the deed in front of a notary, and the affidavit of legal value is completed or an exemption is noted.
  2. Escrow pays your lender and any tax balance out of your proceeds.
  3. The title company checks the deed against the formatting rules: caption, margins, type size and original signatures.
  4. The deed is delivered to Globe or Payson, by mail, in person or by e-recording through a title company.
  5. The Recorder files it and issues a recording number. Keep that number with your closing papers.

Delay at any step pushes the recording date back, which is why it pays to prepare the deed well before the closing day. If the first page is short on top margin, ask the title company to attach a cover sheet rather than retyping the whole deed.

sections.h2: What to ask your title company
sections.html: A few direct questions at the start prevent most problems at the end. Ask which office will receive the deed, Globe or Payson, and whether it will be mailed or delivered by hand. Ask whether your transfer needs the affidavit or qualifies for an exemption, and who will write the exemption on the deed. Confirm that every owner named on the old deed will sign, and that the legal description matches the parcel on your tax bill. If a loan or lien is being paid off, ask when the release will be recorded and whether you will receive a copy.

No lender is involved when the buyer pays cash, so there is no new mortgage to record and no loan conditions standing between you and the filing. The core paperwork remains: a deed signed in original ink, a finished affidavit or exemption note, and a tax balance that has been paid. Ask escrow when the deed will be filed and hold on to a copy.

A house that sat empty, or that came to you through an estate, deserves an early lien search by your title company. Better to learn about an old filing now than at the table.

Central Arizona's Gila County spans 4,795 square miles and holds 53,272 people by the 2020 count, with a 2025 estimate of 53,801. Residents skew older: the median age is 51.7 years, and 29.8% are 65 or older. The county has 32,373 housing units, 31.1% of them vacant, and 75.9% of occupied units belong to the people living in them.

With so many empty houses and an older population, owners here may not see mail or recorded filings right away, which is one more reason to sign up for Fraud Notify. Hayden and Winkelman sit partly in Pinal County, so check which county holds your parcel before you call an office.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Gila County?
faqs.a: At the Recorder's counter in Globe, inside the courthouse at 1400 E Ash St, or in Payson at 707 S Colcord Rd. Both open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

faqs.q: Is the Payson recording office open every weekday?
faqs.a: No. It closes on the fourth Tuesday of each month. Call (928) 474-7139 before you go.

faqs.q: What does the Recorder charge for copies?
faqs.a: Copies are $1 per page. A certified copy adds $3 under state law for the Recorder's certificate and seal.

faqs.q: Does a gift deed need an affidavit of legal value in Gila County?
faqs.a: No. A deed of gift is exempt under A.R.S. 11-1134, as long as the deed states the exemption on its face. Your title company can confirm it for your case.

faqs.q: Can I be alerted when something is recorded against my Gila County property?
faqs.a: Yes. Fraud Notify is free and sends a notice whenever a document is recorded in your name.
